aria: Animated recap of the Mavericks' 130 to 93 home win over Brooklyn: Cooper Flagg's 25-foot jumper with 0.9 seconds left in the first quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 25 points and 12 assists, the top scorers, how the Mavericks won, and the next game against Indiana.
notes: Box score from the Mavericks' 130–93 home win over the Brooklyn Nets on Nov 8, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Dallas Sports Journal, Dallas Hoops Journal (via Yahoo Sports) and the Land of Basketball daily summary. All 130 Mavericks points and all 93 Nets points are accounted for in the box score. The quarter scores are Covers' and match the Dallas Sports Journal's running scores (33–26, 66–46 at the half, 100–71 after three). The 37-point lead and the fact that Brooklyn never led are from Covers and the Dallas Sports Journal. Team totals (points in the paint, rebounds, assists, steals) are Covers'; bench points (58–31) are the Dallas Sports Journal's and match the box score. The Pacers' record and the Mavericks' standing are from the site's standings; the next game and the first meeting are from the Dallas Sports Journal.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cooper Flagg's 25-foot pull-up jumper with 0.9 seconds left in the first quarter, which made it 33–26 (the Dallas Sports Journal; Yahoo's Dallas Hoops Journal calls it a fading three to end the quarter). It capped his 14-point first quarter. It is drawn as a plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Dallas Mavericks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Flagg’s listed 6-foot-9 and 205 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his 7-foot wingspan at the 2025 draft combine (CBS Sports), in the Mavericks' home white with No. 32 (Basketball-Reference). His look hasn't been approved yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
